clue.text: Written evidence leads to convictions

parts.note: a written account kept as evidence, and the police file of past offences that follows a person after being found guilty in court

explanation.surface: Documentary proof in court is what secures guilty verdicts.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a remark about trials, but it plays on the criminal sense of the word: a list of past convictions.
explanation.definitionFit: A document preserving facts is a written log of events, and a criminal one lists someone's past offences.

clue.text: The right are right less often

parts.note: R again abbreviates right
R again abbreviates right

explanation.surface: A political jibe that conservatives are always correct, though the punchline says it happens seldom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The right' and 'right' look like politics and correctness; both are only the letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening less often is more uncommon, the comparative of an adjective meaning infrequent.

clue.text: Stinging bill rises and is cut, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue a word that rises is read from the bottom up, so the bill is turned backwards

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the following letters are only one possible arrangement, so they are shuffled

explanation.surface: A painful invoice goes up and is then trimmed, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' turns AC into CA; 'perhaps' rearranges IS CUT into USTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A biting or corrosive remark or chemical burns, as a sharp criticism or acid would.

clue.text: Yard chase forged and immediately available money

indicators.note: forged means faked or hammered into new shape, so the letters of the two words are remade

explanation.surface: Scotland Yard chases forgers and seizes their funds.
explanation.definitionFit: Money on hand to spend at once is cash in hand, notes and coins ready for use.

clue.text: Dull-witted type taken in by boss

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud on a surface
pi (or pie) is printers' jargon for jumbled type

explanation.surface: A dim person gets swindled by their employer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' suggests an employer, but here it is the ornamental knob on a shield or ceiling; 'type' is printers' slang for jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone slow-witted is foolish, lacking intelligence.

clue.text: Drags children around English capital

indicators.note: the children are placed around, enclosing the other letter

parts.note: tots are small children

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first, upper-case letter

explanation.surface: Someone hauls their kids round London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English capital' suggests London; it is the first letter of English, E, which 'around' places inside TOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry or haul something heavy, an informal verb for lugging.

clue.text: He is found in various coups, making bags of money

indicators.note: various suggests different forms, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A man turns up in assorted takeovers, getting rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges HE with COUPS; 'is found in' and 'making' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: Small sacks for coins are purses, the old leather pockets for carrying cash.

clue.text: Deft clue is an anagram, I included — tricky!

indicators.note: the clue says outright that the words are to be rearranged

parts.note: I is taken as written

explanation.surface: A self-referential clue admits it is a mere jumble and calls itself sly.
explanation.walkthrough: DEFT CLUE has only eight letters; the nine-letter answer needs the I that the clue says is included, lost in the text as held.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dishonest or misleading is crafty and full of trickery.

clue.text: Awakening of love in Laura's development

indicators.note: in places the letter for love inside the rearranged name
development means growth into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its s counted as letters
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A romance blossoms as Laura matures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development' rearranges LAURAS into ARUSAL, and 'in' puts O, love as a tennis score of nil, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rousing from sleep or stirring of feelings is an excitement, a waking up.

clue.text: Resolute enough to put a stop to the bloodshed

definitions.text: put a stop to the bloodshed

explanation.surface: Someone firm enough to end the killing.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the verb, a variant spelling of stanch, to stop blood flowing from a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyal, steadfast supporter is firm; and the verb means to stem a flow of blood.

clue.text: He probably gets pleasure from his craft

definitions.text: He probably gets pleasure from his craft

parts.words: He probably gets pleasure from his craft
parts.note: craft reads as skill, but it is a boat, and pleasure suggests a leisure vessel

explanation.surface: A skilled artisan enjoys his work.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor of a leisure boat enjoys his pleasure craft, the vessel he sails for fun.

clue.text: Delightful move by a footballer in a difficult position

parts.note: pretty means charming or delightful
a pass is a footballer's move sending the ball to a teammate

explanation.surface: A lovely ball played by a player who is under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase a pretty pass is ironic idiom for an awkward state of affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an awkward predicament, a sorry state of affairs.

clue.text: Will him to succeed

parts.note: reads as urging someone on, but will is the legal testament naming who inherits after a death

explanation.surface: Cheer someone on to victory.
explanation.definitionFit: The person named in a testament to take over an estate or title is the successor.

clue.text: Come out with me again and have a drink

indicators.note: again says the shortened word is used twice
out with means the following word is removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to go on another date and have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out with' removes ME from COME, leaving CO; 'again' doubles that to COCO, then add A.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot chocolate beverage made from the powdered bean.

clue.text: She may take the wheel with dazzling effect

definitions.text: She may take the wheel with dazzling effect

parts.words: She may take the wheel with dazzling effect
parts.note: suggests a woman driving, but the wheel is the spinning firework named after a saint

explanation.surface: A woman drives in a showy way.
explanation.walkthrough: A Catherine wheel is a spinning firework; the saint's name is also spelt this way.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name shared with the spinning firework, the saint's wheel.

clue.text: Don't contact workers in their free time

parts.note: hands are manual workers
off means not on duty

explanation.surface: Leave employees alone when they are not at work.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a warning not to touch, a command to keep away.

clue.text: Her charges are small

parts.note: charges seem like fees, but they are children in her care

explanation.surface: A tradeswoman with modest fees.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to look after young children, a nanny.

clue.text: Attributes of the embassy staff?

explanation.surface: Qualities expected of diplomats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attributes' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in assigning blame.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascribe importance is to assign it; and diplomatic officials with a speciality are posted to an embassy.

clue.text: Girl is able to set up a whole lot of dates

parts.note: Alma is a girl's name

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means placed upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: can means is able to

explanation.surface: A girl manages to arrange many romantic outings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns CAN into NAC beneath ALMA. Dates suggests romance; it is the calendar.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearly calendar listing days and events is a book of dates.

clue.text: A revolting subject

parts.note: revolting seems to mean disgusting, but it means rising up, and subject is a citizen of a monarch

explanation.surface: A disgusting topic.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen who rises against the crown is an insurgent.

clue.text: Major acting role in Shaw play

definitions.text: Major acting role in Shaw play

parts.words: Major acting role in Shaw play
parts.note: major suggests a leading part, but it is part of the title of a play by George Bernard Shaw about a Salvation Army officer

explanation.surface: A big part in a Shaw drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The title heroine of Shaw's play Major Barbara is a Salvation Army officer.

clue.text: One always on hand for a date, maybe

explanation.surface: A suitor who is always available for an outing.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the inside of the hand; the second the tree that bears dates, with 'maybe' showing it is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The inside of the hand, and a tropical tree that bears dates.

clue.text: Art of government-utter spin?

parts.note: to utter is to state
spin, artful presentation, is a kind of craft or cunning

explanation.surface: Political governance is nothing but sheer spin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utter' looks like an adjective meaning total; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill in running a nation is the practice of politics and diplomacy.

clue.text: Measures taken to decorate indoors?

explanation.surface: Steps one takes when painting a room.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the stepladder a decorator uses inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Actions taken are moves; and a folding ladder is used when painting a room.

clue.text: Sweets for kids

explanation.surface: Desserts made for children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kids' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in teases; a fool is also a fruit-and-cream dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Creamy fruit puddings are desserts; and to kid someone is to trick or tease them.

clue.text: Explorer, one given all-round support

indicators.note: being given something all round means being surrounded by it

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar
taken as written

explanation.surface: An adventurer is backed up on every side.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is someone who goes first into new territory, a trailblazer.

clue.text: Fine example of quiet part of Spain

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
Aragon is a region of north-east Spain

explanation.surface: A model of Spanish tranquillity.
explanation.definitionFit: A model of excellence is a perfect example.

clue.text: Remove from duty

explanation.surface: Exempt someone from obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the verb to cut out; the second the tax on goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut something out surgically is to remove it; and a tax on goods is a levy.

clue.text: Ladies make perfect models

indicators.note: make suggests the letters form something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Women who become flawless fashion models.
explanation.definitionFit: Standards of perfection are exemplars worth aspiring to.
